title: Mariology
description: Introductory self-study with source readings, case exercises and knowledge checks.
creditNote: 20 internal formation credits. Non-accredited education; not a qualification, licence or evidence of competence to practise counselling, psychology or psychotherapy.

units.title: Mary in salvation history
units.label: Educational study
objectives: Read Marian passages within the story of Christ and Israel.
Apply the lesson to the case study and explain the limits of your conclusion.
paragraphs: Begin with Luke 1–2, reading the whole scene before selecting a verse. Notice who speaks, what God promises and how Mary responds. Her consent belongs within God’s initiative of grace; it does not make her the source of salvation. John 2 and John 19 place her within the public ministry and Passion of her Son. Acts 1:14 places her among the praying disciples.

Biblical typology recognizes patterns across the story of salvation. It differs from treating every detail as a secret prediction. When studying Genesis 3:15 or Isaiah 7:14, first describe the passage in its own setting, then explain the Church’s reading in relation to Christ. Keep three columns in your notes: the biblical text, its ecclesial interpretation and your personal reflection. This simple distinction prevents a devotional insight from being mistaken for a direct biblical quotation.
units.assignment: A friend says every mention of a woman in the Bible directly predicts Mary. Write a respectful response using Luke 1 and the difference between context and typology.

quiz.question: What is the best first step when studying Luke 1:28?
options: Read the surrounding Annunciation narrative.
Ignore the surrounding narrative.
Treat a devotional image as the biblical text.
quiz.explanation: Context helps identify what the passage actually says.

quiz.question: What does sound typology require?
options: A hidden meaning for every word.
Replacement of the literal sense.
Attention to both the earlier context and its relation to Christ.
quiz.explanation: Typology connects the biblical story without erasing its historical sense.

units.title: Theotokos: Mother of God
units.label: Dogma
objectives: Explain why the title Mother of God is a statement about Christ.
Apply the lesson to the case study and explain the limits of your conclusion.
paragraphs: The title Theotokos, commonly rendered Mother of God, safeguards the identity of the one whom Mary bore. Jesus Christ is one divine Person, truly divine and truly human. Mary is mother of this Person according to his human birth. The title does not mean she created the divine nature, existed before God or is mother of the Father and the Holy Spirit.

The Council of Ephesus in 431 defended this confession in a controversy about how to speak of Christ’s unity. Start with the question “Who is Jesus?” before asking what the title says about Mary. In a catechetical explanation, keep person and nature distinct without dividing Jesus into two persons. Read Luke 1:43 alongside the Catechism. An accurate sentence about Mary should deepen, rather than compete with, the confession that the Word truly became flesh.
units.assignment: Explain Theotokos to a teenager who thinks the title means Mary created God. Include the distinction between person and nature.

quiz.question: The title Theotokos chiefly safeguards what?
options: Mary’s existence before the Trinity.
A divine nature belonging to Mary.
The unity and divine identity of Christ’s Person.
quiz.explanation: The one born of Mary is the eternal Son incarnate.

quiz.question: Which explanation is accurate?
options: Jesus is two separate persons.
Mary bore the divine Son according to his humanity.
Mary originated the divine nature.
quiz.explanation: Her motherhood concerns the Person born, without making her the origin of divinity.

units.title: Perpetual virginity
units.label: Dogma
objectives: Distinguish Catholic doctrine from claims about human dignity or marriage.
Apply the lesson to the case study and explain the limits of your conclusion.
paragraphs: Catholic teaching confesses Mary as ever-virgin. Study the Catechism’s presentation alongside Matthew 1 and Luke 1 rather than making the doctrine rest on one translated word. Biblical references to the brothers of Jesus require attention to language, context and the Church’s received interpretation. A short slogan is not a substitute for that study.

The teaching concerns Mary’s particular vocation and the identity and mission of her Son. It does not imply that marriage, sexuality within marriage or other mothers are impure. Avoid speculative anatomical descriptions; the purpose of the doctrine is theological. When discussing it with another Christian, first state fairly what that person believes. Then distinguish the shared confession of Christ’s virginal conception from the further Catholic confession of Mary’s perpetual virginity. Patient explanation is more useful than accusations about someone’s faith.
units.assignment: A catechist says Mary’s virginity proves married people are less holy. Correct the claim while explaining the Catholic doctrine respectfully.

quiz.question: Which inference should a catechist reject?
options: That the doctrine should be read in context.
That marriage or married mothers are impure.
That Mary has a particular vocation.
quiz.explanation: The doctrine does not reduce the dignity of marriage.

quiz.question: How should disputed biblical expressions be studied?
options: Through language, context and the Church’s interpretation.
By choosing a single English word without context.
By guessing details about anatomy.
quiz.explanation: Sound interpretation requires more than an isolated phrase.

units.title: Immaculate Conception
units.label: Dogma
objectives: Explain Mary’s preservation from original sin as a gift of Christ’s grace.
Apply the lesson to the case study and explain the limits of your conclusion.
paragraphs: The Immaculate Conception refers to Mary’s conception, not to Jesus’ virginal conception. Catholic teaching holds that from the first moment of her existence Mary was preserved from original sin by a singular grace of God, in view of the merits of Jesus Christ. She is redeemed by Christ; she is not an exception to humanity’s need for a Saviour.

The definition in Ineffabilis Deus (1854) must be distinguished from the earlier theological debates that helped clarify the question. The idea of preservative redemption explains how saving grace can prevent a fall rather than only restore someone after it. This is an analogy for understanding the doctrine, not an account of a medical process. When making a study chart, separate the definition, its theological explanation and later devotional expressions. A feast, an image and a doctrinal definition each communicate in a different way.
units.assignment: Write a short response to: “If Mary was immaculately conceived, she did not need Jesus to save her.” Explain which conception the doctrine concerns.

quiz.question: Whose conception is named in this doctrine?
options: Mary’s.
Only Jesus’ birth in Bethlehem.
The conception of every disciple.
quiz.explanation: The Immaculate Conception is about Mary’s preservation from original sin.

quiz.question: How does this teaching relate Mary to Christ?
options: She saves herself independently.
She replaces Christ as redeemer.
She receives a unique gift of his saving grace.
quiz.explanation: Preservative redemption still depends entirely on Christ.

units.title: Assumption and Christian hope
units.label: Dogma
objectives: Connect Mary’s bodily glorification with Christian resurrection hope.
Apply the lesson to the case study and explain the limits of your conclusion.
paragraphs: The Assumption teaches that Mary, at the completion of her earthly life, was taken body and soul into heavenly glory. The definition in Munificentissimus Deus (1950) does not settle every historical question about the manner of the end of her life. Avoid filling those gaps with a narrative presented as part of the defined dogma.

Distinguish Assumption from Christ’s Ascension, while keeping both within the saving action of God. Mary’s glorification points towards the destiny promised to the Church; it is not permission to neglect embodied life on earth. Care for a sick person, respect for the body and hope for the resurrection belong together. In studying Revelation 12, recognize the richness of the woman’s imagery and its ecclesial context. Do not present the chapter as if it were a modern eyewitness report of the Assumption.
units.assignment: Prepare a funeral-related explanation of resurrection hope that neither invents details about Mary’s death nor promises a grieving family immediate relief.

quiz.question: What does the dogma affirm?
options: Every detail of Mary’s last earthly day.
That human bodies have no lasting value.
Mary was taken body and soul into heavenly glory.
quiz.explanation: The definition concerns her bodily glorification, not every historical detail.

quiz.question: What pastoral practice is consistent with this hope?
options: Neglecting the sick because only souls matter.
Caring for people’s bodily needs while offering hope.
Dismissing grief as a lack of faith.
quiz.explanation: Christian hope respects embodied persons and does not cancel grief.

units.title: Mary as New Eve
units.label: Educational study
objectives: Use patristic comparison without treating Mary as an independent saviour.
Apply the lesson to the case study and explain the limits of your conclusion.
paragraphs: The New Eve comparison contrasts disobedience with Mary’s obedient response to God. Early Christian authors such as Irenaeus use this pattern within their account of Christ restoring humanity. Its centre is the new Adam, Christ. Mary’s cooperation is made possible by grace and remains subordinate to his saving work.

A patristic text needs a date, author and context. Do not attribute every Marian saying circulated online to a Church Father. Consult the linked patristic library and identify the actual work before quoting. Typological comparison also has limits: Eve and Mary are real figures within different biblical settings, not interchangeable symbols. In a study exercise, name the point of comparison and then one difference. This makes an explanation more precise and guards against using an evocative image as if it proved every later theological claim.
units.assignment: Explain the New Eve comparison using one similarity, one contrast and one limit. State why Christ remains central.

quiz.question: What is the centre of the New Eve comparison?
options: The replacement of the Gospels by a legend.
Christ’s saving work and Mary’s grace-enabled cooperation.
A second independent source of salvation.
quiz.explanation: The comparison belongs inside the account of Christ’s redemption.

quiz.question: Before quoting a Father online, what should you do?
options: Locate the work and examine its context.
Assume the image caption is a reliable citation.
Add quotation marks to a paraphrase.
quiz.explanation: A traceable primary text is necessary for accurate attribution.

units.title: Mary and the Church
units.label: Educational study
objectives: Explain Mary as a model of faith within the communion of the Church.
Apply the lesson to the case study and explain the limits of your conclusion.
paragraphs: Mary is presented in Catholic teaching as a member of the redeemed community with a unique vocation, and as a model of the Church’s faith, hope and charity. Her presence with the disciples in Acts 1 can guide reflection on a community receiving the Spirit together. She does not draw the Church away from Christ or make ordinary disciples unnecessary.

Read a Marian image alongside a concrete act of discipleship. For example, listening to God’s word can become patient study; faithful presence can become accompanying someone in difficulty. These are applications, not additional dogmas. A parish that honours Mary should also welcome people whose prayer styles differ. Personal preference for one devotion is not a reliable measure of another person’s holiness. The Church’s sacramental life, care for neighbours and common confession of faith provide a wider setting for Marian prayer.
units.assignment: Plan a Marian parish activity with one scriptural reading, one work of mercy and an invitation that does not pressure people to adopt your preferred devotion.

quiz.question: Which practice reflects Mary as a model of the Church?
options: Listening to God and practising charity together.
Ranking holiness by a favourite private devotion.
Removing Christ from the centre of worship.
quiz.explanation: Marian formation should nourish ecclesial faith and love.

quiz.question: A practical application of a doctrine is what?
options: Automatically a new defined dogma.
A replacement for the source text.
An application that should be identified as such.
quiz.explanation: Keep the authority of a source distinct from your proposed application.

units.title: Intercession and Christ’s unique mediation
units.label: Educational study
objectives: Describe intercession without making Mary a rival to Christ.
Apply the lesson to the case study and explain the limits of your conclusion.
paragraphs: Christ is the one mediator between God and humanity. Catholic prayer asking Mary or other saints to intercede is understood as participation in the communion of Christ, not as access to a competing power. At Cana, Mary directs attention towards Jesus. A careful explanation begins with him and keeps every created cooperation dependent on grace.

Different Marian titles have different histories and levels of authority. Do not assume that frequent devotional use makes a title a dogma, and consult current guidance from the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith when discussing disputed terminology. In pastoral conversation, a person may bring a request directly to God; Marian intercession is not a barrier that must be crossed before God will listen. If someone fears that an exact number of prayers is necessary to obtain care, respond with the freedom and trust of Christian prayer rather than reinforcing a transaction.

The 2025 doctrinal note Mater Populi fidelis judges “Co-redemptrix” inappropriate for defining Mary’s cooperation, because it can obscure Christ’s unique saving mediation. Read its discussion of Marian titles before teaching them. Mary’s maternal intercession remains entirely dependent on Christ; it is not an independent source of saving grace.
units.assignment: Answer a person who thinks God will not hear them unless they first complete a Marian devotion. Explain intercession and the freedom to pray directly to God.

quiz.question: How is Marian intercession understood in Catholic teaching?
options: As a rival source of divine power.
As a condition before God can hear any prayer.
As dependent participation in Christ’s unique mediation.
quiz.explanation: All authentic intercession depends on Christ.

quiz.question: How should a disputed Marian title be assessed?
options: Assume all titles carry equal authority.
Check its meaning and current magisterial guidance.
Treat its popularity as a definition.
quiz.explanation: A title’s use and its doctrinal weight must be distinguished.

units.title: Devotion, liturgy and worship
units.label: Devotional practice
objectives: Distinguish veneration of Mary from adoration due to God.
Apply the lesson to the case study and explain the limits of your conclusion.
paragraphs: Catholic tradition distinguishes adoration, due to God alone, from the honour given to saints and the special veneration of Mary. The terms latria, dulia and hyperdulia can help, but an explanation should still use ordinary language. Mary is a creature redeemed by God; she is not a member of the Trinity.

A devotion should lead towards Christ, Scripture, the sacramental life and love of neighbour. The Rosary meditates on the mysteries of Christ with Mary. A novena is a pattern of prayer, not a mechanism for compelling a result. When choosing a devotional text, identify its source and keep the wording faithful while distinguishing source claims from Church teaching. Practice can be adapted to someone’s health and capacity without shaming them. A missed day need not become a reason for fear, and a prayer routine must not replace necessary medical or psychological care.
units.assignment: Design a short introduction to the 54-day novena that explains veneration, Christ-centred prayer and freedom from guaranteed-result claims.

quiz.question: To whom is adoration due?
options: Every saint in the same sense as God.
God alone.
Mary as a fourth divine person.
quiz.explanation: Catholic teaching distinguishes adoration from veneration.

quiz.question: Which introduction to a novena is appropriate?
options: An invitation to persevering prayer and trust.
A guarantee of a job on day 54.
A replacement for needed healthcare.
quiz.explanation: Devotional discipline is not a guarantee or a substitute for care.

units.title: Discernment of private revelation
units.label: Private revelation and discernment
objectives: Distinguish public Revelation, devotional accounts and ecclesial discernment.
Apply the lesson to the case study and explain the limits of your conclusion.
paragraphs: The Christian confession centres on God’s definitive Revelation in Jesus Christ. Private revelations do not add a new deposit of faith or correct the Gospel. Their possible pastoral value must be distinguished from the duty to believe revealed doctrine. A moving story, a large following or a claimed miracle does not by itself establish supernatural origin.

The Church has procedures for examining alleged supernatural phenomena. Read the current norms and the actual decision for a particular case; do not translate a limited pastoral permission into a claim that every message is guaranteed by the Church. Look carefully at what a document does and does not decide. In everyday formation, avoid spreading frightening predictions, unverified promises or collective blame for Christ’s Passion. Use reliable sources, respect the dignity of all people and allow room for prudent non-participation in a private devotion.
units.assignment: A prayer website calls an unverified apparition “required Catholic belief.” Write a correction distinguishing public Revelation, private revelation and the wording of Church decisions.

quiz.question: Can a private revelation replace or complete Christ’s Revelation?
options: No.
Yes, when its website is popular.
Yes, if it offers a new required Gospel.
quiz.explanation: Private revelations do not add to the deposit of faith.

quiz.question: What should you do with an alleged approval?
options: Assume it verifies every associated message.
Ignore the distinction between doctrine and devotion.
Read the actual decision and its scope.
quiz.explanation: Discernment requires the precise language and scope of the decision.
